sentence: This project tests whether neuron-targeted caveolin-1 protects motor neurons in the brain and spinal cord of mice with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
This project measures hazardous organic compounds and metal concentrations in human blood, animal tissues, and soil from superfund sites.
This project tests how a meditation that focuses on positive feelings changes brain-based and subjective effects of pain in patients with chronic low back pain.
This project studies how a receptor helps a signal drive inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis, using synovial fibroblasts from patients and preclinical models.
This project studies the molecular mechanisms by which a cytokine drives dedifferentiation of epithelial cells in the intestines.
This project tests whether human monoclonal antibodies from skin-based antibody-secreting cells can reduce herpes shedding and reactivation in animal models.
This project looks for microbial microproteins that control macrophages, a cell type involved in controlling human cancer cells.
This project builds an ultrasound system that uses deep learning to detect emboli automatically over long time periods in patients at risk.
This project builds a nuclear magnetic resonance spectrometer that uses a laser and microwave with diamonds in a microfluidic chip to measure metabolic concentrations.
This project tries to find out how visceral adipose tissue leads to endothelial dysfunction in obesity.
This project studies how germ cells develop in planarians, a simple animal where genes are easy to identify and study.
This project tries to find out how red light increases blood flow by releasing nitric oxide from endothelial vesicles.
This project creates artificial cell interfaces to learn how cells signal to the extracellular matrix and to other cells, using fibroblast and T cell models.
This project develops a tool that uses artificial intelligence and large language models to collect clinical data for animal models of rare genetic diseases.
This project works to improve the mechanical and optical properties of bioengineered corneal tissues made from a patient's own adult stem cells.
This project brings together cancer research to improve prevention, detection, diagnosis and treatment of cancer.
This project studies how oxidative stress and redox imbalance in the brain cause injury in neonatal mouse models after oxygen deprivation.
This project develops an artificial intelligence approach to remove motion blurring from CT images of the beating heart and study plaque buildup.
This project tests whether low levels of a glutamate receptor in brain astrocytes contribute to alcohol dependence behaviors in mice.
This project builds an experimental system to test how gene-environment interactions cause differences in susceptibility to chemical exposure.
